Yes, when you use `pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>`, the entire virtual environment, including all the installed packages, will be deleted.

A virtual environment created with `pyenv virtualenv` is a self-contained Python environment with its own set of installed packages and dependencies. When you delete the virtual environment using `pyenv virtualenv-delete`, the entire directory containing the virtual environment is removed, including all the installed packages.

After deleting the virtual environment, you won't be able to access or use the packages that were installed within that environment. If you need to preserve the installed packages, you should consider exporting the package list to a requirements file before deleting the virtual environment, and then re-creating the environment and installing the packages from the requirements file later.
